phases.name: Walking Skeleton — Devon deletes an all-unique HF folder end-to-end
phases.description: Thinnest end-to-end vertical slice that proves the architecture for folder-group delete: modeltap-core grows the FolderGroup / FolderDeletePlan / FolderDeleteOutcome / Sidecar types and the Tool::delete_folder trait method (default Err(DeleteError::Unsupported)), the HF plugin implements the happy-path override for an all-unique folder (sidecar enumeration + per-file unlink loop + empty-tree cleanup), modeltap-tui adds the folder-header row type, the [+]/[-] indicator, the Shift+F keymap entry, and the folder-confirm dialog, modeltap-app orchestrates the plan + dispatch + post-action LastAction. Exit gate = the M1 @walking-skeleton scenario in folder-group-delete.feature passes against a real HF tempdir fixture using the real HF plugin override. Closes the riskiest assumption (the trait extension is source-compatible AND the per-file unlink + empty-tree cleanup is correct) before any confirmation safety or partial-failure work begins.
phases.release_target: Release 3 — Folder-group delete (sub-release of parent Release 2 'Reclaim disk safely')
phases.exit_gate: The M1 walking-skeleton scenario 'Devon deletes an all-unique HF repo folder and reclaims disk' in docs/feature/folder-group-bulk-delete/distill/features/folder-group-delete.feature passes on macOS and Linux CI, AND the workspace continues to satisfy `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`, and `cargo test --workspace` (parent regression gate INT-FGD-8 partial preview).

steps.name: Core types and Tool trait extension (FolderGroup, FolderDeletePlan, FolderDeleteOutcome, Sidecar, DeleteError::Unsupported, Tool::delete_folder default body)
steps.description: Lands the algebraic types and the trait surface that every later step composes against. Adds FolderGroup, Sidecar, SidecarKind, FolderClassification (with SharedModel), and FolderDeletePlan to modeltap-core::types per data-models.md sections 1–4. Adds the DeleteError::Unsupported { tool: ToolId } variant to the existing DeleteError enum and ensures every existing exhaustive match compiles (the compiler enforces the update across modeltap-app and the plugins). Extends the Tool trait in modeltap-core::tool with the seventh method `async fn delete_folder(&self, plan: &FolderDeletePlan) -> Result<Vec<DeleteOutcome>, DeleteError>` whose default body returns Err(DeleteError::Unsupported { tool: self.name() }). FolderGroup's smart-constructor invariants (path regex, absolute_path naming convention, model tool == hf, sidecars-may-be-empty) are enforced by construction. FolderDeletePlan's invariants (paths counts, classification counts, reclaim+retain==total within rounding) are unit-tested directly. No behavior change to existing plugins — Ollama / llama-cli / lm-studio inherit the default body and compile without source changes. Pure-logic-only step; no I/O, no async edges touched yet.

steps.name: Pure folder-group logic (group_by_hf_repo, classify_unique_vs_shared, build_folder_delete_plan) — single-engine invariant enforced at the call site
steps.description: Lands the pure-function surface in modeltap-core::logic::folder_group per component-boundaries.md §'New module: modeltap-core::logic::folder_group' and the C4-L3 in architecture-design.md §4.3. Three functions: group_by_hf_repo partitions HF ToolInventory.models by the `<author>/<repo>` prefix of id_in_tool and pairs each group with the sidecars supplied by the HF plugin; classify_unique_vs_shared routes EVERY child model through compatibility::compute_indicator and projects the result into FolderClassification (Shared → shared with other_tools; Compatible | FormatLocked | Unknown → unique per data-models.md §3 mapping table); build_folder_delete_plan computes paths_to_unlink_fully (unique models + all sidecars), paths_to_unlink_hf_only (shared models' HF-side paths), bytes_to_reclaim, bytes_to_retain, and asserts the reclaim+retain==total invariant. The single-engine invariant (AC-13 / D-FGD-4) is enforced at the call site: classify_unique_vs_shared is the ONLY producer of FolderClassification and its body MUST call compute_indicator for each model. No I/O, no async, no tokio in this module.

steps.name: HF plugin override for the all-unique happy path (delete_folder, enumerate_sidecars, delete_folder_at, remove_empty_repo_tree)
steps.description: Lands the HF plugin's Tool::delete_folder override for the simplest case: all-unique model files plus sidecars, no EBUSY, no shared files. Wires plugins/hf::folder_delete::HfPlugin::delete_folder to wrap the sync work in tokio::task::spawn_blocking per the existing ADR-005 pattern. Implements enumerate_sidecars(repo_dir) — owned by the HF plugin per AC-14 / B-FGD-2 — using walkdir to find README.md, .imatrix, .gguf.urls, and HF-internal refs/blobs entries scoped to this repo's snapshot. Implements delete_folder_at(hub, plan) — the per-file unlink loop — that routes model files through the existing crate::delete::delete_one_at (reusing ADR-009 ref-counting) and sidecars through direct std::fs::remove_file, collecting one DeleteOutcome per file. Implements remove_empty_repo_tree(repo_dir) — best-effort cleanup of the now-empty models--<author>--<repo>/ directory tree. The contract from architecture-design.md §4.4 and ADR-010 §Implementation Guidance applies: per-file failures continue (no early return) but the walking skeleton only exercises the all-success path. No partial-failure work in this step (that lands in phase 04). No shared-file classification yet beyond the unique-only happy path (that work lands in phase 03). The exact sidecar suffix list is a software-crafter decision per architecture-design.md §13 open item and component-boundaries.md §Open items deferred to DELIVER.

phases.name: Confirmation safety — typed-confirm guardrails (mismatch, Esc, trailing slash, non-HF no-op)
phases.description: Builds out the four safety guardrails around the typed-confirm dialog from milestone M2 in folder-group-delete.feature. Each guardrail asserts that the destructive path is unreachable when the user has not entered byte-exact confirmation, and that the cancel paths leave the filesystem byte-identical. Wrong-path mismatch, Esc cancellation, trailing-slash mismatch (D2 decision: byte-exact, no normalization), and Shift+F no-op when the active tool is not Hugging Face (the [F] indicator dimmed in the bottom bar). No new architecture — extends the dialog state machine and the keymap with the cancel/no-op branches. The pre-action inventory snapshot mechanism (DirManifest per step-definitions-skeleton.md §H) is materialized here so 'no destructive action' assertions are byte-precise.
phases.exit_gate: All four M2 scenarios in folder-group-delete.feature pass with @skip removed; the K-FGD-3 mis-target rate guardrail invariant (zero filesystem mutation on aborted dialog) holds across the four scenarios.

steps.name: Wrong-path mismatch + trailing-slash mismatch + Esc cancellation (byte-exact comparator, DirManifest pre/post assertion)
steps.description: Wires the three cancel paths into the dialog state machine. The comparator is byte-exact and case-sensitive per AC-8 / D2; any input not equal to folder_group.path (including trailing slash) cancels with no destructive action and emits JSONL action.folder_delete event with outcome == cancelled_mismatch. Esc cancels at any point with outcome == cancelled_escape. Materializes the DirManifest fixture helper (recursive (path, size, mtime) snapshot of the HF cache root) so the 'no files removed' / 'fixture directory is byte-identical' assertions are byte-precise rather than file-count-equal. Un-skips three M2 scenarios in folder-group-delete.feature. No HF-plugin-side changes — the cancel paths are entirely in modeltap-tui (dialog) + modeltap-app (orchestrator's reject-and-emit path).

phases.description: Promotes the all-unique walking-skeleton path to the full mixed case: a folder containing both unique-to-HF model files and files hardlinked into Ollama (and possibly other tools). Reuses the ADR-009 reclaim-math + delete_one_at ref-counting for per-file unique-vs-shared accounting; the dialog itemizes 'N unique + M shared + K sidecars' and reports 'Reclaim X GB' (unique + sidecars) and 'Retained Y GB (M file(s) also linked in <tool>)'. The cross-tool hardlink survival (INT-FGD-4) is asserted via stat-equality of inodes before and after delete. The @property scenario (M3 / AC-13) is implemented as a proptest per D6 — for any generated FolderGroup, classify_unique_vs_shared's output matches compute_indicator on every child. steps.name: Cross-tool hardlink survival end-to-end (INT-FGD-4) + plugin-contract S.2 / S.6 (HF supported)
steps.description: Wires the HF plugin's delete_folder override for the mixed case: shared files have only their HF-side path unlinked (paths_to_unlink_hf_only); unique files are fully unlinked (paths_to_unlink_fully). Crucially, the existing delete_one_at ref-counting from ADR-009 is the load-bearing mechanism — when a shared file's HF-side path is unlinked, the blob remains because another tool (Ollama) still references the same inode. Verified end-to-end by the M3 'Folder-delete preserves the Ollama-side hardlink for a shared model file' scenario (@destructive @real-io against devon-hf-mixed fixture with stat-equality of inodes pre and post). Also stands up the plugin-contract test 3.11.S.2 (mixed shared and unique) and 3.11.S.6 (preserves cross-tool hardlinks) per plugin-contract-spec.md — the HF plugin's own contract test transitions from happy-path-only to the full Supported capability path. phases.name: Partial failure — per-file detect-and-retry, EBUSY simulation seam, post-action partial summary
phases.description: Implements the partial-failure path per ADR-010 § Concurrency and D-FGD-6 / AC-12. The HF plugin's delete_folder iterates the plan's paths sequentially; per-file failures (EBUSY, permission denied, NotFound) are captured as DeleteOutcome { registration_removed: false, file_deleted: false, bytes_freed: 0 } and the loop continues without early return. Adds the MODELTAP_TEST_EBUSY_PATHS env-var seam per D4 — gated behind cfg(any(test, feature = "test-harness")) in the HF plugin's delete_one_at wrapper so production builds are unaffected. The post-action LastAction summary itemizes successes and per-file failures with reasons. The 'Press [F] again after closing ollama to finish' hint is rendered when the partial-failure outcome contains EBUSY entries. Idempotent retry (re-running Shift+F on the now-shorter folder header after closing the offending tool) succeeds against the remaining files. Also adds the integration-checkpoint pre-flight refusal scenarios (AC-15 read-only cache; AC-20 folder vanished out-of-band) since they share the orchestrator's pre-flight machinery.

phases.name: Plugin-contract boundary — Layer A + Layer B Unsupported for Ollama / llama-cli / lm-studio
phases.description: Asserts the trait extension's source-compatibility property end-to-end across both the unit-layer (Layer B plugin contract) and the user-observable layer (Layer A E2E). Layer B: each non-HF plugin's tests/folder_delete_contract.rs declares FolderDeleteCapability::Unsupported and asserts that delete_folder returns Err(DeleteError::Unsupported { tool: plugin.name() }) and that no filesystem mutation occurs. Layer A: the M5 Scenario Outline parameterized over plugin ∈ {ollama, llama-cli, lm-studio} asserts the orchestrator's surfacing of the Unsupported error — either as the user-observable text '<plugin> does not support folder-delete' or as a JSONL no-dispatch event, per D5 fallback. This is the safety net for the future-5th-plugin case (US-18 / K4 / ADR-010 § Consequences): an Atomic Chat plugin (or any other) added in a future PR must add its own folder_delete_contract.rs entry, defaulting to Unsupported unless folder semantics are explicitly added.
